issues.problem: The per-scene targets (official results/MipNeRF360 c3 csv for garden/bicycle/counter) cannot be compared with the paper's 7-scene averages, and c3 is not the config behind the paper's size. 7-scene means from the repo csvs: c3 = 28.50 dB / 0.853 / 0.212 / 25.55e6 B (24.37 MiB); c1 = 28.49 / 0.853 / 0.212 / 28.83e6 B (27.49 MiB). Paper Our-FT: 28.61 / 0.856 / 0.206 / 27.62 MB. So the paper size matches c1 in MiB, not c3, and even the authors' own released csvs are ~0.1 dB / 0.006 LPIPS short of the paper. The paper's MB is MiB (official code divides by 1024^2); the plugin's size_MB is MiB while the requested metric is bytes/1e6 (4.9% apart).
issues.evidence: csv bytes/1e6 vs /2**20 (computed); mesongs.py save_npz prints zip_file_size/1024/1024; paper_results.json mixes 'size_MB' paper values with csv bytes.
issues.fix: Run all 7 paper scenes (bicycle bonsai counter garden kitchen room stump) for the paper comparison, c3 and c1. Compare to the repo csv per scene for the 3 pilot scenes. Convert units explicitly (report both MiB and 1e6). Never score against the paper 7-scene mean with 3 scenes. Treat repo csv as the achievable ceiling and the paper as not reproduced by the authors' own release.

issues.problem: Official training_report returns the TEST PSNR of the last mode loop, so the saved 'best' model is argmax test PSNR over 20 evals (every 400 iterations up to 8000; the variable is misnamed psnr_train). Not doing this and scoring the final model is the right call; selection on test is leakage, and here validation aliases test so there is no clean held-out split. Provenance of the csv rows (final vs best vs a render.sh decode of bins.zip) is unknown, so the targets may be optimistically biased by a small amount.
issues.evidence: mesongs.py training(): cur_psnr > psnr_train -> scene.save_ft('best'); training_report psnr_val is overwritten by mode 'test'.
issues.fix: Keep final-model scoring as primary. Optionally log a diagnostic test PSNR every 400 iters and label it 'oracle-best, not a result'. Do not select on it.

issues.problem: The adjoint-by-other-transform backward is exact only if I(F(x)) = x. I confirmed orthonormality, round trip and both adjoint identities on 200k points at depth 20 (one edge voxel, 0 bad rows, adjoint inner products agree to 1e-7). The reproduced edge quirk (voxel code 2^depth, morton keeps 20 bits) can break the round trip when several points sit on the max edge. The count is computed but never written to the compress record, and the raht probe uses codes < 2^depth, so it never exercises that case at scale.
issues.evidence: density.compress record has no roundtrip_bad_rows; probes.raht uses rng.integers(0, 2**depth).
issues.fix: Add roundtrip_bad_rows to the compress record and fail or warn if > 0 on real scenes. Add an edge-voxel case to the raht probe.

issues.problem: Scale LR is multiplied by the runtime scene_scale, which equals the official cameras_extent only with --recipe 3dgs. The default recipe uses a 0.9-quantile point radius, so a run without the flag silently changes the scale LR (and the means LR).
issues.evidence: runtime.py: recipe '3dgs' -> camera_extent, else quantile. bench_request passes --recipe 3dgs but nothing enforces it.
issues.fix: Record scene_scale in the compress record and check it against the dataset camera extent, or document it as mandatory.

issues.problem: (imp/imp.max())[:n] is then divided by its own max inside vq_features, while the official divides the full-length imp by the full max. Only the absolute scale of S differs, which matters only through eps=1e-5 and is negligible.
issues.fix: Pass imp and slice after normalisation inside vq_features, or accept.

issues.problem: np.linspace dtype follows numpy version for float32 scalar endpoints (float64 on numpy 1.x, float32 on numpy 2). At depth 20 this shifts voxel boundaries slightly relative to the official environment.
issues.evidence: Both the official and this code pass np.float32 min/max to np.linspace.
issues.fix: Pin to float64 explicitly and note it; the effect on key counts is tiny.

issues.problem: White background (training, eval and compositing) while the released script and csv targets use black. Importance (alpha*T) is background independent, but the baseline checkpoint, fine-tune and eval differ from the targets.
issues.fix: Keep as a documented gap and compare drop vs the same-protocol baseline, not absolute dB.

issues.problem: Only a 2000-step smoke run (23.06 dB vs 23.07 for the baseline, 5.95 MB) and tiny probes exist. No 30k+8k run, so the 8000-step fine-tune, per-scene LRs and full-scale RAHT and VQ memory and time are unvalidated. Sampling is with replacement (official shuffled stack).
issues.fix: Run garden first and compare to csv 26.39 dB / 42.94e6 B / 3.10M Gaussians before the other scenes.

probe_assessment.why: Compares with one-hot compositor oracle from the same rasteriser, checks the invisible Gaussian and the quantile rule. It cannot detect a gsplat-vs-official-CUDA semantic difference, but the thresholds (0.99, 1/255, T<1e-4) match.
Compared against a line-by-line port of octreecodes; forced duplicates exercise the merge.
Compared with the verbatim port, round trip, norm, DC, smooth-signal compaction and adjoint vs autograd. The edge-voxel case is not covered.
Formula check per block plus STE and running range.
Checks R(euler(q)) = R(q) and that swapping the argument order fails.
Decoded render equals bank render (2e-4), members listed, scales are quantised.
Asserts prune count, voxelisation, positions fixed, codebook and opacities move, last step frozen, 4 codebook steps, encode ran.

fidelity_gaps_confirmed: Own gsplat 3DGS base (white background) instead of the authors' checkpoints
Final model, not best-by-test every 400 iterations (correct to omit)
gsplat rasteriser for importance and rendering
Euler sqrt clamp; decoded model renders via quaternions recovered from the Euler matrix
FT length 8000 from the mic script; fine-tune lengths for other scenes are not published
Size reported as MiB by default; request is bytes/1e6
summary: Code-level fidelity to the official MesonGS is high: I found no critical or major implementation deviation in importance, voxelisation, RAHT, block quant, Euler, VQ, fine-tune schedule or bitstream, and I verified the RAHT orthonormality/adjoint claims numerically at depth 20. The major issue is the benchmark protocol: targets come from c3 csv rows on 3 scenes while the paper's 27.62 MB / 28.61 dB 7-scene averages match c1 in MiB, and the authors' own csvs do not reach the paper. Run 7 scenes, report both size units, and score the final model. No full-scale run exists yet, so the quirk counters and the fine-tune are unvalidated.
